text: Let us recap. Three definitions of acids and bases, each wider than the last. Conjugate pairs differ by one proton, and a strong acid has a weak conjugate base. Alpha is root K over C. K w is ten to the minus fourteen, and K a times K b equals K w. p H is minus log hydrogen ion, and for a weak acid hydrogen ion is root K a C. K s p links to solubility, and when Q exceeds it, a precipitate forms. A common ion suppresses ionisation. A buffer follows Henderson's equation. An indicator must change inside the jump. And salts hydrolyse according to which partner is weak.
